headline: Day three: the AI tape bounced (NDX +1.35%, momentum +3.4%) as desks sized the data-center hit at a few percent and called the hedge-fund unwind mostly done, but retail and systematic supply keep a second low on the table.
market_read: The narrative moved from 'how bad' to 'how much is really at risk': Bernstein (Rezaei, 6 Nov) puts only 2-4% of the credible US pipeline at real risk and MS (McVeigh via Wigg/Risom, 6 Nov) 4.9 GW of IT load in 2028 (~4% of cumulative capacity), against SIG's (Hosseini, 6 Nov) 60 GW 'delay' bucket and the WSJ-cited 25-45% claims. Positioning is cleaner: MS PB (via Wigg, 6 Nov) has L/S net leverage at 42%, bottom decile, cut entirely by long selling, and QDS (Metli) thinks the HF unwind is nearly complete. But retail and systematics are the swing: QDS still sees $30-40bn of systematic supply and expects a bounce then a new low, and UBS's Cheong (via Dwyer, 6 Nov) eyes a Monday-morning washout. The first upside optionality showed up (UBS Ruple, 6 Nov: NVDA call spreads, MSFT upside, a SOXX put spread sold), while LOs and HFs both kept selling semis and industrials into the close (BofA Villani/Fenske, 6 Nov).

up.why: JPM's Schilsky (6 Nov) says to chase APP after +31% on the day and +50% in a week: still ~50% down YTD and Axon 3.0 is rolling out; JPM's global specialists carry it as a TMT long with short interest at 4% of float (research is Neutral). Monitor: APP HOT 70.6 and BULL 71.7, both in the 60-80 band; in its own history that HOT band was followed by a +2.3% median 5-session move (n=12) and +2.7% over 10 sessions. 1-5 days: momentum after the print in a tape that still sells AI-capex names. 2-4 weeks: whether ad-tech is treated as a non-capex AI winner.
up.confirm: Holds gains if the semis bounce fails; more sell-side upgrades of 2027 EPS toward the 'low $20s' bull case.
up.weaken: Unity takeout talks (SLP/PIF) reframed as a competitive threat; the AI tape sells everything again.

up.why: Desks call it the cleanest software print of the cycle (Jefferies Favuzza, 6 Nov: Q4 guide ~38% y/y, a long lean into the print); TMTB (6 Nov) instead says positioning had come down into it, so the beat met lighter positioning. BofA (Villani, 6 Nov) puts it in 'infrastructure gains vs application pains'. NET is not in the Bloomberg-X mover list or the analog set, so this rests on desk evidence. 1-5 days: follow-through after a +15-20% day. 2-4 weeks: whether infrastructure software becomes the AI-adjacent long that rotators pick.
up.confirm: More upward estimate revisions; infrastructure peers (DDOG, SNOW, MDB) firm in sympathy.
up.weaken: Valuation pushback (Jefferies' Gallo stays Hold; Bernstein MP) and a broad tech de-gross.

up.why: BofA's desk (Villani, 6 Nov) lists Arista's beat/raise on hyperscaler scale-across among the week's strongest demand signals. Monitor: Bloomberg-X attention z +1.87 (Δ +2.43) with the biggest tone gain in the universe (+0.35); HOT 78.6 and BULL 81.6. Caution: in ANET's own history the 60-80 HOT band was followed by a -3.7% median 5-session move (n=9), so a hot read here has not paid short-term. 2-4 weeks: whether networking is separated from the 'DC delay' basket.
up.confirm: Holds while the semis basket retests; desk talk of LO buying in networking.
up.weaken: Another leg of AI-infra liquidation; MSFT or META capex trims.

up.why: BofA (Villani, 6 Nov) credits the Scorpio switch ramp across hyperscalers for a big beat, and BofA research (Arya via Fenske, 6 Nov) names ALAB among best-of-breed networking in its base case. Monitor: Bloomberg-X Δ +2.14, HOT 74.8, BULL 69.3, after -27% over 7 sessions and -45% over 28; its own HOT-band history shows an +11.6% median 5-session move but on only 7 cases. 1-5 days: a high-beta rebound candidate if the bounce holds. 2-4 weeks: depends on whether the market stops pricing 2028 GW risk into networking.
up.confirm: Holds a rebound through the systematic-supply window (Fri-Mon).
up.weaken: New low in the SOX next week, as QDS expects.

up.why: Bernstein spec sales (Seidman, 6 Nov) and research (Chhugani via Patafio, 6 Nov) both lean positive after the print: AI cloud revenue +182% q/q, $20bn backlog, ~1.4 GW of approved capacity still to sell, a ~90% customer prepayment easing financing; the stock had fallen ~70% since June. The offset is the MSFT delivery slipping to February. IREN is not in the monitor analog set. 1-5 days: post-print squeeze (+15% pre-market). 2-4 weeks: whether neocloud financing fears (Barclays, Wood) override the company-specific story.
up.confirm: More prepayment-funded contracts; CRWV's print next week shows no customer pullback.
up.weaken: Further MSFT pullback from third-party DC projects (Nscale precedent).

down.why: The crowded memory long is still being sold rather than rebuilt: Jefferies' desk (Favuzza, 6 Nov) says semis, memory and semicaps have been continually for sale for four weeks, with the 5 Nov skew toward long-onlies; MS (Wigg, 6 Nov) had global memory -14.5% and WDC/STX ~60% off highs; UBS (Gaudois, 6 Nov) says crowding has receded across APAC tech and Samsung/SK Hynix at 0.79x/0.98x 2028E P/BV price a downcycle. Divergence: BofA's desk calls memory demand 'A+', Arya flags MU's buyback starting 9 Dec, and Mohan says SNDK has 67% of FY28 bits contracted with price floors. Monitor: MU HOT 49.2 (mid-band; +1.7% median 5-session after this band, n=26); SK Hynix Bloomberg-X attention falling (Δ -1.89). This is easing crowding, not a weaker fundamental read.
down.confirm: Desks report LO selling in memory continuing after the bounce; Korea/Taiwan margin deleveraging continues.
down.weaken: LO buying returns to memory around MU's buyback start or a strong DRAM contract-price print.

down.why: The December-quarter guide (-1% q/q vs Street +1%) and a light EPS number turned a strong September quarter into -10-13%; Jefferies' desk (Favuzza, 6 Nov) felt a short lean into the print and BofA research (Arya via Fenske, 6 Nov) trimmed FY28 EPS 4% and cut the PO to $80. Curtis (Jefferies) calls the cyclical tailwinds 'in the rearview mirror'. MCHP is not in the monitor analog set. 1-5 days: shorts were positioned, so covering can cause chop. 2-4 weeks: analog peers (TXN, ADI, ON) read across.
down.confirm: More estimate cuts; analog peers lag in the bounce.
down.weaken: Backlog improves on March/June capacity adds, as management flagged.

down.why: BofA (Fenske, 6 Nov) lists NOW among software names having a rough quarter against expected guides, and the desk frames it as 'application pains' while infrastructure gains. Monitor: NOW had the largest Bloomberg-X attention drop in the universe (z -0.93, Δ -3.44), HOT 30.8; its own history in this band shows a -1.9% median 5-session move (n=11). Falling attention here reads as neglect, not crowding being cleared. 2-4 weeks: no catalyst until the 9 Dec event.
down.confirm: Application-software peers keep missing high bogeys (TEAM -16%).
down.weaken: Rotation into beaten-down quality software as AI infra stays volatile.

down.why: Neocloud financing remains the soft spot: Barclays' desk (Kantrowitz, 6 Nov) says MSFT backed out of an Nscale deal and that smaller levered players with breakable contracts are most at risk; UBS (Ruple, 6 Nov) relays MSFT stepping away from risky DC projects; Jefferies' Wood (6 Nov) sees no appetite to lock rentals beyond one year. Bernstein (Rezaei, 6 Nov) disagrees for CRWV in Texas specifically (contracted through 2027), and neoclouds bounced +9% pre-market (TMTB, 6 Nov). Monitor: CRWV HOT 36.8 and BULL 33.8 (20-40 band); its own history shows a +11.9% median 5-session move from this band, but on only 5 cases. CRWV reports next week (UBS calendar).
down.confirm: More hyperscaler pullbacks from third-party capacity; wider neocloud credit (see AI Credit alerts).
down.weaken: A CRWV print that reaffirms backlog and financing; MSFT/OpenAI capacity reconfirmed.

down.why: JPM's Adler (6 Nov) names MRVL, ~40% lower since the LITE deal announcement, as a stress point that had the AI trade teetering before the election; Jefferies (Curtis, 6 Nov) counters after a two-day NDR that scale-in production pulls into 2028-29 and LITE already has five NPO designs, while acknowledging investor frustration with a large deal in this tape. MRVL is not in the monitor analog set. 1-5 days: high beta to the semis bounce. 2-4 weeks: MRVL's own print and deal-financing details.
down.confirm: Deal arbitrage or financing overhang keeps it lagging optical peers in rebounds.
down.weaken: Optical (COHR, LITE) leads the rebound and drags MRVL with it.

themes.title: Sizing the data-center hit: the numbers differ by base
themes.text: Bernstein (Rezaei, 6 Nov) sees the credible at-risk pipeline rising from 78 to 105 GW, of which ~17 GW could face tighter rules, so 2-4% of the credible pipeline (pipeline GW) is realistically lost. MS (McVeigh via Wigg and Risom, 6 Nov) puts 4.9 GW (IT load) at risk in 2028, 4% of cumulative capacity, and 12.4 GW through 2030, with no 2027 risk. SIG (Hosseini, 6 Nov) has 60 GW of 148 GW of training-focused AI DC projects at risk of delay and 12 GW canceled in a worst case. Tech Fund (7 Nov) relays a GS figure of ~45% of planned capacity facing delays or oversight, and Brad Gerstner's 25-35% of next year's build. These bases (credible pipeline GW, IT-load GW, project GW, share of plans) are not comparable; the desk consensus is that the sell-off priced more than the sell-side sizings.

themes.title: Is the unwind done? Hedge funds yes; retail and systematics are the swing
themes.text: MS PB (via Wigg, 6 Nov) has L/S net leverage at 42% after a top-5 one-day drop since 2005, driven entirely by long selling; QDS (Metli) thinks the HF unwind is nearly complete but expects a bounce then a new low, with $30-40bn of systematic supply left. UBS (Dwyer, 6 Nov) puts risk-control selling at $200-270bn over two days, and Cheong sees a possible Monday washout. UBS (Ruple, 6 Nov) sees the first call buying (NVDA, MSFT) and a SOXX put spread sold. BofA (Villani/Fenske, 6 Nov) saw the 5 Nov close flip to net buying with record retail ETF purchases, but LOs and HFs both kept selling semis and industrials. MS's Wilson (via Amerian/Risom, 6 Nov) sounded outright bullish on an entry point but wants a marginal new low first; one UBS client called it a regime change.

themes.title: Inside the AI trade: networking/optical, memory and app software are treated differently
themes.text: Desks are separating the AI complex. Fundamentals in networking and optics are called intact: BofA's desk (Villani, 6 Nov) cites ANET, ALAB and COHR (2027 fully booked, a new NPO LTA into 2028), and Jefferies' MRVL/LITE NDR (Curtis, 6 Nov) pulls scale-in into 2028-29. Memory is cheap but still being sold (Jefferies, UBS). In software, infrastructure (NET, FROG) is gaining while applications (TEAM, NOW) are the pain trade (BofA Fenske, 6 Nov).

themes.title: Contrarian voices: peak capex and a Huang headline
themes.text: Jefferies' Christopher Wood (GREED & fear, 6 Nov) argues that markets are signalling an unwillingness to fund AI and revives his call that AI capex could peak this year, pointing to AI credit spreads/CDS and to neocloud rentals that are not locked beyond one year. Separately, Tim Culpan (Culpium, 7 Nov, independent author) relays NYT/FT reports on alleged Chinese intelligence targeting of Jensen Huang; Nvidia calls the interactions normal customer meetings. It is a headline risk for NVDA's standing in Washington rather than a fundamental claim.

observations.excerpt: CRWD was lower than plan, growing LSD y/y, but it sounded like this partner may have lost some share and is lapping a strong October 2025 quarter
observations.subject: U.S. Software: Security Partner Call: Datapoints on PANW, ZS, CHKP, CRWD, OKTA

coverage_gaps: No DAMNANG or SemiAnalysis mail arrived in the window (6 Nov 11:02Z to 7 Nov 13:00Z), so there is no quality-source semis read today.

Several primary notes sat behind links and were read only as sales summaries: Bernstein (Rezaei) DC note, MS McVeigh capacity model, BofA Arya trough analysis and Mohan scenarios, UBS HOLT hyperscaler note, GS Pasquariello/George Lee podcast (link only).
MS Wigg's 'CRWV NBIS preview' and Jefferies' TX data-center section were cut off by the 12k-character body limit.
Saturday window: little new desk mail after 6 Nov 23:50Z (MS Friday Five); Monday-open positioning (UBS's washout scenario) is not yet observable.
source_notes: Channel: Outlook desktop COM (desk_mail_collect.ps1); inbox lag 0.2 h; 607 messages screened, 233 bodies retrieved, ~41 read for this review.
Mail window 2026-11-06T11:02Z (prior to_utc minus 2 h) to now; newest received 2026-11-07T12:52Z (GS Pasquariello).
Fubon's Taiwan margin-debt comments reappeared via Jefferies' Rankie Wong (6 Nov); they were already counted in the 6 Nov review (via O'Mara), so they were not re-logged as new observations.

Editorial weighting: desk/specialist voices (no ratings) are weighted as positioning colour; research relays are labelled with the analyst's name. TMTB, Vital Knowledge, Tech Fund and Culpium are independent authors, not brokers. Bloomberg-X and analog figures are taken from monitor.json (through 2026-11-06), not recomputed.
